§12.1.3 Logos

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

images-logos · images furniture

✅ Normative

A logo MUST be rendered as a marker carrying its printed words, [logo: OSTREVANE], at the logo's place in reading order. A logo that prints no legible text MUST be rendered as [logo]. The artwork MUST NOT be described.

Almost every slide and letterhead carries one: a wordmark in the corner, a symbol beside it, sometimes a faint version behind the content. The marker keeps the printed words (never drop) and tells a reader that they are a brand mark rather than a word of the body text.

Requirements

  • The words a logo prints MUST appear inside the marker exactly as printed, case included: [logo: VELTRAND LIFE]. A wordmark set on two lines is one marker, its lines joined with a space.
  • The marker sits at the logo's place in reading order. A logo inside a header or footer band stays inside that band — see Recurring Page Furniture§4.6.
  • A logo with no legible text — a symbol on its own — is the bare [logo].
  • A symbol printed beside its own wordmark is part of that logo; it does not get a second marker.
  • A faint copy of a mark repeated behind the content is not a second logo and adds nothing; it MUST NOT break into the table or paragraph it lies behind. A faint background mark that carries words is a watermark — see Watermarks§7.3.13.
  • The artwork — colours, shapes, the apple — MUST NOT be described.

✅ Sample — a corner wordmark and a background mark

The wordmark OSTREVANE with a yellow apple symbol sits in the bottom-right corner of the footer band, and a large faint version of the same apple sits behind the lower (CAPEX) table. The background apple is a faint repeat of the mark and adds nothing to the table; the wordmark becomes [logo: OSTREVANE] in the footer band. Expected boxes: the CAPEX table as one Table box; the footer band as page furniture, with the wordmark inside it.

✅ Sample — two stacked wordmarks on a slide

VELTRAND PROVIDENCE (set on two lines) and VELTRAND LIFE, each a red box with a white diamond symbol, top-right. Each wordmark is one marker; the two-line one joins its lines with a space. The slide's map is a real map with a two-entry legend — see Geographic Maps§12.2.4; it is elided here. Expected boxes: one box per wordmark.
